frames: A player on a court in a ready stance seen from the side, facing the net. The feet are shoulder width apart with the knees bent, holding the racket with both hands in front of the body at waist height, the head up looking at the ball.
Backswing: the shoulders turn sideways to the net and the racket is taken back behind the right hip. The left arm points forward, the weight on the back foot and the knees bent, the eyes on the ball.

Follow-through: the racket has swung forward and up over the left shoulder after contact. The weight is on the front foot, the hips and shoulders rotated to face the net, the right arm wrapped across the body and the ball flying forward.
Tennis.note: A forehand groundstroke with a full swing and a high follow-through over the opposite shoulder.

Badminton.equipment: a badminton racket, a shuttlecock, a net
frames: A player in a ready stance seen from the side, the knees bent and the feet wide apart. The racket is held up in front of the body with the right hand at chest height and the left hand out for balance, the eyes on the shuttle above.

Preparation: the player jumps back with the racket cocked behind the head, the elbow bent high and the body arched back. The left arm points up at the shuttlecock above and the knees are bent. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Badminton clearly in this side (facing right) view.

Smash: at the top of the jump, the right arm extends and the racket strikes the shuttle overhead, the wrist snapping down. The body is rotated forward, the left arm drops to the chest and the feet are in the air.
Badminton.note: An overhead jump smash with the racket contacting the shuttle at full arm extension.

Squash.equipment: a squash racket, a small rubber ball, a walled court
frames: A player in a squash court seen from the side, standing in a ready stance near the center line. The knees are bent, the racket is held up in front at chest height with the wrist cocked and the eyes watching the ball on the wall.

Backswing: the player steps toward the side wall with the right leg and rotates the shoulders. The racket is taken back above shoulder height with the wrist cocked and the elbow bent, the left arm out for balance.

Follow-through: the racket swings forward and contacts the ball low and ahead of the body. The player lunges on the front leg with the knee bent, the racket arm extended along the wall and the eyes on the ball.
Squash.note: A forehand drive with a lunge toward the front wall, with the racket wrist cocked.

Cricket.equipment: a cricket bat, a cricket ball, pads, helmet and stumps
frames: A batsman at the crease in a ready stance seen from the side, wearing pads and a helmet. The feet are shoulder width apart with the knees slightly bent, the bat held with both hands and its blade resting on the ground, the head turned toward the bowler.

Backswing: the batsman lifts the bat back above the right shoulder, the left elbow high. The weight shifts onto the back foot and the front shoulder points toward the bowler while the eyes are on the ball.

Follow-through: the bat swings down through the ball and finishes high over the left shoulder, the arms extended. The front foot has stepped forward with the knee bent, the weight is on the front leg and the head is over the ball.
Cricket.note: A straight drive with the front foot stepping toward the ball and the bat finishing high.

Rugby.equipment: a rugby ball, boots, a pitch
frames: A rugby player running with the ball seen from the side, the ball held in both hands at the right hip. The torso leans slightly forward, the knees are bent in a stride and the eyes are up looking at the field.

Passing: the shoulders rotate to the left and the ball is swung across the body in both hands. The hips are turned, the arms are extended in front and the player continues running. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Rugby clearly in this side (facing right) view.

Release: the player's arms extend fully sideways and the ball is released from the hands toward a teammate on the left. The torso is rotated and the arms follow through, the legs in stride and the eyes on the receiver.
Rugby.note: A spin pass thrown across the body to the side while running, with both hands on the ball.

frames: A player standing close to the net seen from the side, the knees bent and the arms down. The eyes are on the ball tossed above and ahead, the weight on the toes ready to jump.
Jump: the player leaps up with the legs extended and the left arm pointing up at the ball. The right arm is cocked back behind the head with the elbow high and bent, the back arched.

Spike: at the top of the jump the right arm swings over and the open hand strikes the ball above the net, the arm extended. The body is rotated forward, the left arm drops to the chest and the feet are in the air.
Volleyball.note: An attack spike with a high arm contact and the ball above the net.

Table Tennis.equipment: a table tennis paddle, a small ball, a table with a net
frames: A player standing at the end of a table seen from the side in a ready stance, the knees bent and the feet wide. The paddle is held in front at waist height with the right hand and the eyes on the ball.

Backswing: the shoulders turn to the right and the paddle is taken back behind the right hip. The knees are bent, the weight is on the back foot, the left arm is bent in front for balance and the eyes on the ball.

Follow-through: the paddle swings forward and up in front of the face after hitting the ball. The weight shifts onto the front foot, the hips and shoulders rotate toward the table and the right arm finishes bent near the left shoulder.
Table Tennis.note: A forehand loop with a short compact swing and the paddle finishing near the opposite shoulder.

Golf.equipment: a golf club, a golf ball on a tee
frames: A golfer addressing the ball seen from the side, standing with the feet shoulder width apart, the knees flexed and the torso bent forward from the hips. Both hands grip the club with the clubhead resting behind the ball, the arms hanging straight.

Top of the backswing: the shoulders turned about 90 degrees away from the target with the back facing the target. The arms are lifted and the club is overhead, pointing about parallel to the ground, the left arm straight, the knees flexed.

Finish: the club has swung through the ball and ends high over the front shoulder. The hips and chest face the target, the weight is on the front foot with the back heel lifted, and the body is balanced upright.
Golf.note: A full swing with the chest turned fully away at the top and facing the target at the finish.

Boxing.equipment: a heavy bag, boxing gloves, hand wraps
frames: A boxer in a fighting stance seen from the side, the left foot forward and the right foot back with the knees bent. Both gloves are up by the chin, the elbows are tucked in to the ribs and the chin is tucked down.

Mid jab-cross: the left glove has shot straight out at shoulder height and the right hand begins to rotate. The hips begin to turn, the back heel pivots and the chin remains tucked behind the left shoulder.

Finish of the cross: the right arm is fully extended at shoulder height hitting the bag, the hips and shoulders rotated square. The back heel is lifted and pivoted, the left glove is back at the chin and the weight is on the front foot.
Boxing.note: The hands return to guard at the chin and the chin stays tucked, with the cross driven by hip rotation.

Kickboxing.equipment: a pair of boxing gloves, shin guards and a kick pad held by a partner
frames: A kickboxer in a fighting stance seen from the side, the left foot forward and the right foot back, the knees bent. Both gloves are up by the chin, the elbows tucked in, the chin down and the weight evenly spread.

Chambering the kick: the athlete pivots on the left foot and the hips rotate. The right knee lifts and bends to about 90 degrees across the body, the guard remains up at the chin and the torso leans back slightly.

Roundhouse contact: the right leg extends in a wide arc and the shin strikes a pad held at the waist height. The standing foot pivoted with the heel toward the target, the hips rotated, the torso leaning away and the guard up.
Kickboxing.note: A roundhouse kick landing with the shin, with the standing foot pivoted and the hands staying up.

Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.equipment: a pair of grappling partners in gi on a mat
frames: Two athletes in white gi on a mat seen from above. One partner is on the back with the legs wrapped around the other in a closed guard, the other kneeling between the legs of the first with the hands gripping the lapel.

The athlete on the back breaks the posture of the partner by pulling the head down with the hands on the collar. The hips lift and rotate toward the side, the legs open and one leg moves up to the partner's shoulder.

Submission: the athlete on the back has the legs and arms controlling the partner's arm in an armbar. One leg over the partner's chest, the other over the face, the hips raised and the partner's arm extended against the hips.
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.note: The two grapplers wear gis, and the arm bar is shown in control without any strike.

Wrestling.equipment: a wrestling mat, singlets and wrestling shoes
frames: Two wrestlers in singlets face each other in a staggered stance seen from the side, knees deeply bent. The hands are up in front at chest height, the torsos are leaning forward and the heads are close together.

The shot: one wrestler lowers the level and lunges forward with the lead knee to the mat, arms reaching to wrap behind the opponent's knees. The head is up against the opponent's ribs and the back is straight.

Takedown finish: the attacking wrestler drives forward with the legs and lifts the opponent's legs off the mat. The opponent is tipped backward toward the mat, the attacker's head is tight to the ribs and the arms clasp behind the knees.
Wrestling.note: A double-leg takedown with a level change, a straight back and the head up against the ribs.

Judo.equipment: a pair of athletes in judo gi on a tatami mat
frames: Two judoka in judo gi face each other seen from the side, each gripping the other's sleeve and lapel. The knees are slightly bent, the torsos are upright and the feet are shoulder width apart. The head is faceless and neutral, in line with the spine, with every limb position readable from this side (facing right) view of the Judo.

Entry: the thrower pulls the opponent forward with the sleeve and the lapel, steps in and turns the back to the opponent. The hips drop below the opponent's hips and the knees bend as the thrower pivots.

Throw: the thrower bends forward, the opponent is lifted over the thrower's back and is rotating in the air toward the mat. The thrower holds the sleeve with one hand, the legs are straight and the hips are above the opponent.
Judo.note: A hip throw with the thrower's hips lower than the opponent's, and the grips on the sleeve and lapel.

Karate.equipment: a karate gi and black belt on a dojo floor
frames: A karateka in a white gi stands in a front stance facing the camera, the left leg bent forward and the right leg straight behind. The left arm is in a block position in front and the right fist is chambered at the hip.
Mid technique: the hips rotate forward as the right fist begins to travel straight out from the hip. The left hand pulls back to the left hip, the back leg stays straight and the stance stays low.

Finish: the right fist is fully extended at chest height in a straight punch, the wrist twisted palm down. The left fist is chambered at the left hip, the front knee is bent deeply and the back leg straight, the eyes forward.
Karate.note: A reverse punch in a deep front stance, with the opposite fist chambered at the hip.

Skateboarding.equipment: a skateboard and a flat skate park surface
frames: A skater standing on a skateboard seen from the side, the front foot over the front bolts and the back foot on the tail. The knees are bent in a crouch, the arms are out slightly, the board on the ground.
Pop: the skater snaps the back foot down on the tail and the board tilts up with the nose rising. The knees are bent deeply, the arms swing up and the front foot slides up the board.
In the air: the skater and the board are above the ground with the board level under the feet. The knees are bent and drawn up, the arms are out wide for balance and the eyes are looking ahead.
Skateboarding.note: An ollie with both feet staying on the board, which rises level beneath them.

Surfing.equipment: a surfboard on a breaking ocean wave
frames: A surfer paddling prone on a surfboard seen from the side on an approaching wave, the chest lifted off the board with the arms stroking in the water. The legs are straight and the board is angled toward the shore.

Pop-up: the surfer pushes up with both hands on the board near the chest and the feet jump under the body. The back foot lands near the tail and the front foot in the middle of the board with the knees bent.

Riding: the surfer stands on the board in a low crouch, the front knee bent over the front foot and the back leg bent over the tail. The arms are out for balance, the shoulders are turned toward the wave and the board rides across the wave face.
Surfing.note: The pop-up goes from prone to a crouched stance with the feet on the board's stringer line.

Snowboarding.equipment: a snowboard with bindings, boots, and a snowy slope
frames: A snowboarder standing on a snowy slope seen from the side, the feet strapped into the bindings across the board. The knees are bent, the weight is slightly on the front foot and the arms are out for balance.

Carving: the snowboarder leans into the turn with the body tilted. The board is on its edge, the knees are bent deeply, the front arm points down the slope and the back arm is out, the head turned downhill.
Exit of the turn: the board flattens out and the snowboarder rises with the knees extending. The arms are out wide, the shoulders are parallel to the board and the snow sprays from the board's edge.
Snowboarding.note: A carved turn with the board on its edge and the knees bent, with a rider facing sideways on the board.

Skiing.equipment: a pair of skis, ski poles, ski boots, a snowy slope
frames: A skier on a snowy slope seen from the side, both skis parallel and the ski poles held at the sides, the arms bent in front. The knees are bent, the torso leans slightly forward and the weight is over the center of the skis.

Turn initiation: the skier plants the downhill pole and rises slightly, then the skis begin to tilt on their edges. The knees angle into the turn, the hips are shifted and the upper body faces downhill.

Carving: the skis are fully on edge in a carved arc, the knees angled deeply into the turn and the torso facing down the slope. The outside ski is weighted, the poles are held out and the snow sprays from the ski edges.
Skiing.note: A parallel carved turn with a pole plant, both skis staying parallel.

frames: A dancer standing in a ready pose facing the camera, the feet together and the arms relaxed by the sides. The knees are slightly bent, the chest is lifted and the head is up. The head is faceless and neutral, in line with the spine, with every limb position readable from this front view of the Dancing.

Mid step: the dancer steps to the right with the right foot as the right arm sweeps up and out to the side at shoulder height. The left arm bends across the chest, the hips shift to the right and the torso tilts slightly.

Finish: the dancer is on the balls of the feet in a spin with both arms extended wide at shoulder height. The right leg is lifted with the knee bent and the toes pointed to the side, the torso is upright and the head is up.
Dancing.note: A single expressive step and arm sweep into a turn, with an upright torso and open arms.

Martial Arts Class.equipment: a mat floor, uniforms, and several students in a row
frames: A row of students in white uniforms stands facing the camera in a ready stance, the feet shoulder width apart. The fists are held at the hips, the backs are straight and the instructor stands in front of the row.

Mid technique: the students step forward with the left leg into a front stance in unison. The right fists begin to extend from the hips and the left arms are pulled back to the sides. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Martial Arts Class clearly in this front view.

Finish: all students hold a front stance with the right arm extended in a straight punch at chest height. The left fists are chambered at the hips, the front knees are bent and the back legs are straight in a straight line.
Martial Arts Class.note: All the students move in unison, and the instructor stands at the front of the line.

frames: A person standing at the front of the yoga mat in mountain pose facing right, the feet together and the arms by the sides. The back is straight, the head is neutral and the palms face forward.

Moving into the pose: the athlete steps the left foot back about a metre into a lunge and the arms sweep overhead. The front knee is bent at 90 degrees over the ankle and the back leg is straight with the heel lifted.

Warrior hold: the athlete has the front right knee bent at 90 degrees and the back left leg straight with the foot flat on the mat. The arms are extended overhead with the palms together, the torso is upright and the gaze is forward.
Yoga.note: A warrior I pose with the front knee over the ankle and the back foot angled on the mat.

frames: A person lying on their back on a Pilates mat seen from the side, the knees bent and the feet flat on the mat. The arms rest by the sides and the head rests on the mat, the spine neutral.

Rolling up: the athlete lifts the head and shoulders off the mat and the legs rise to a tabletop position with the knees bent at 90 degrees above the hips. The arms reach forward beside the thighs and the belly draws in.

The Hundred: the head and shoulders are lifted off the mat, the legs are extended at about 45 degrees to the floor. The arms are straight at the sides, pumping a few centimetres above the mat, and the abdominals are drawn in.
Pilates.note: The Hundred is shown with the legs extended at 45 degrees and the lower back pressed into the mat.

frames: A person standing tall facing right with the feet together and the arms by the sides, the knees straight. The head is neutral and the back is straight. The head is faceless and neutral, in line with the spine, with every limb position readable from this side (facing right) view of the Stretching.

Folding: the person hinges forward from the hips with the knees straight and the back flat, the arms reaching toward the floor. The chest moves toward the thighs and the head hangs forward. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Stretching clearly in this side (facing right) view.

Full hold: the torso is folded forward over the straight legs with the head toward the shins, the hands resting on the floor or the shins. The knees are straight, the weight is over the balls of the feet and the hips are above the ankles.
Stretching.note: A standing forward fold with a hinge at the hips, with the knees straight and the neck relaxed.

frames: A person on hands and knees on the mat seen from the side in a table position, the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips. The back is flat and the head is neutral.

Cat phase: the spine rounds up toward the ceiling, the head drops toward the chest and the hips tuck under. The arms stay straight and the hands and knees stay in place. Keep the faceless head neutral and aligned with the spine, and show every joint angle of the Mobility Flow clearly in this side (facing right) view.

Cow phase: the spine arches down, the chest lifts and the tailbone tilts up while the head lifts to look forward. The arms stay straight and the hands and knees stay in place. The faceless head stays in line with the spine, and the limb angles of the Mobility Flow must read clearly from the side (facing right) view.
Mobility Flow.note: A cat-cow spinal flow with the hands and knees fixed, and the spine moving through its full range.
